The *Ekasaṅkhiyattheraapadāna* is a canonical verse text located in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Following the standard pattern of Apadāna literature, it records the past spiritual deeds and aspirations of an elder (*thera*) that culminated in final liberation in the present life [SuttaCentral]. Five modern translations across five languages are recorded for the text on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
Automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 111 matching passages shared between this poem and 43 other Pali compositions [DharmaNexus]. The concluding segments (§10–§15) in particular show high textual overlap with recurring stock verses found throughout the *Therāpadāna*, such as the *Ucchaṅgapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 419), *Pāṭihīrasaññakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 435), *Uttarattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 558), and *Ekapattadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 504), along with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects cross-linguistic formulaic alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan literature, including the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* and *Tathāgatabimbakārāpaṇasūtra*, as well as the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* and *Saddharmānusmṛtyupasthāna*, though these machine matches reflect shared narrative and verse phrases rather than established textual parallels [DharmaNexus].
